[1/5] Plan: harden post-audit code — combined-label helper, duration policy constants, export cancellation, corrupt-config quarantine, boundary tests, CI workflow

impact_assessment.why: Post-delivery analysis of HEAD found acknowledged-but-unimplemented gaps (cancel-event comment in export loop), duplicated combined-label logic at 3 call sites, two disagreeing duration policies, silent loss of corrupt config, and missing boundary tests for rules added in 510d2da
impact_assessment.benefits: Single source of truth for category labels and duration bounds; exports no longer outlive the app or produce unrequested files; corrupt config preserved for recovery; new validation rules regression-protected; CI runs the 4s suite on every push
impact_assessment.risks: contract: _run_export_thread gains optional cancel_event param, callers checked (1 site) -- no other consumers; dependency: CI installs requirements.txt pinned already -- no new deps; concurrency: cancel event set from Tk main thread while export thread polls -- threading.Event is the safe primitive, file write happens once after loop; state: quarantine renames a corrupt config to .corrupt -- never overwrites an existing quarantine without timestamp; tests must not spawn audio threads (sounddevice mocked/stubbed as in existing suite)
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests before each behavior change; keep UI-layer reject and thread clamp aligned via shared constants; cancellation only stops file writing, no partial WAV; quarantine uses timestamped suffix; CI workflow uses windows-latest to match the desktop target

[1/2] Adopt from MoriNo23 fork: tests/conftest.py deterministic import environment + per-file mock alignment (numpy/scipy always real)

impact_assessment.why: Empirically verified: our suite fails 14 tests when pytest collects files in a different order (per-file MOCK_MODULES race); the new CI plus any future ordering change makes this a real flakiness risk. The MoriNo23 fork (fetched from their push 2026-10-19) diagnosed the same problem and shipped conftest.py; their version alone left 13 failures in reversed order because their per-file blocks still mock numpy
impact_assessment.benefits: Order-independent test suite; real numpy/scipy in every test regardless of collection order; standalone file runs keep working; baseline for later adoption of the fork's strobe feature tests
impact_assessment.risks: contract: conftest imports before test modules -- files keep their guarded sys.modules installs so standalone runs still work; dependency: none new; concurrency: none (test-only); state: tests/conftest.py is a new untracked file -- review ensure not accidentally left uncommitted
impact_assessment.mitigation: Verification runs the suite in normal AND reversed file order; failing order-dependence was reproduced first (14 failed); keep edits test-file-local, zero SourceCode.py changes
